study_type.claude: Mixed methods (concurrent embedded: survey with PLS-SEM/IPMA plus thematic analysis)
study_type.nlm: Mixed methods (concurrent embedded: survey with PLS-SEM/IPMA plus thematic analysis)
study_type.note: Survey-based theoretical model plus qualitative analysis of open-ended responses.

research_method.claude: Concurrent embedded mixed methods: large-scale survey analysed with PLS-SEM (CFA/EFA psychometric refinement of PICSE) and IPMA, plus reflexive thematic analysis of open-ended responses; 238 valid of 343 responses; 386 qualitative responses
research_method.nlm: Concurrent embedded mixed methods: survey with PLS-SEM and IPMA, EFA/CFA psychometric evaluation, reflexive thematic analysis; N = 238; 386 open-ended responses
research_method.value: Concurrent embedded mixed-methods design: cross-sectional survey (TXAI, PICSE-derived items, GenderMag facets, UTAUT; 5-point Likert) analysed with PLS-SEM after EFA/CFA refinement of PICSE, plus IPMA; reflexive thematic analysis of 386 open-ended responses on challenges and risks
research_method.note: The 343 received responses are reported only by Claude (not contradicted).

context.claude: Industry; professional developers at GitHub Inc. and Microsoft; 238 valid responses (Microsoft 154, GitHub 84)
context.nlm: Industry; professional developers at GitHub Inc. and Microsoft; N = 238 (GitHub 84, Microsoft 154)
context.value: industry; professional software developers at GitHub Inc. and Microsoft; 238 valid survey responses (Microsoft 154, GitHub 84)

ai_discussed.note: Developers' trust in and adoption of genAI tools is the topic.

remote_covid.note: Work mode not specified by either; no mention of remote work or COVID-19 in the full text.

cat_productivity.note: Productivity not measured; 'Functional value' (labelled Productivity by both) is a perceived survey construct, which goes to Survey.

cat_quality.note: Perceived System/Output quality of genAI (consistent accuracy, safe and secure practices, style matching, presentation, performance); genAI-induced technical debt discussed qualitatively.

cat_satisfaction.note: Borderline: both classify trust in genAI (TXAI scale) as Satisfaction; frustration reported only qualitatively.

cat_activity.note: Both label self-reported genAI usage frequency 'Activity / Adoption', but it is not repository activity.

cat_devex.note: NotebookLM labels many constructs 'DevEx' and Claude labels ease of use and goal maintenance 'DevEx', but the Noda/Storey/Forsgren DevEx framework is not used.

cat_survey.note: All constructs measured by Likert survey; open-ended responses analysed qualitatively.

evidence.quote: We addressed these goals through a concurrent embedded mixed-methods design [34], combining a large-scale survey analyzed with PLS-SEM and IPMA with qualitative analyses of participants' open-ended responses.
After excluding non-analytic responses (e.g., "N/A", off-topic or vague remarks), we retained 386 responses: 206 on challenges and 180 on risks.
The final sample retained 238 responses (Microsoft: 154; GitHub: 84) spanning six continents and a wide range of SE experience.
We developed a theoretical model of developers' trust and adoption of genAI using a large-scale survey (N = 238) conducted at GitHub and Microsoft.

System/Output quality reflects genAI's presentation, safety and security practices, performance, and output quality-including the consistency and correctness of outputs relative to developers' styles and workflows (S2-S5, E3).
In this study, we used the validated Trust in eXplainable AI (TXAI) instrument [67, 109] to assess developers' trust in genAI tools.
Shallow solutions and repetitive failure loops wasted time, added frustration, and forced participants to abandon or work around the tool.
All closed-ended questions used a 5-point Likert scale
